subject to change. However, guidance supports a passage through

morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant sea heights
reaching as high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi.

properties.instruction:

force conditions Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions
are expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely
dangerous for any vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi
approaches the Marianas, stay in safe harbor.

properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 16 at 4:11PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHAMPI MOVING RAPIDLY WEST ON APPROACH TO THE
MARIANAS...
...CHAMPI LIKELY TO MOVE NEAR GUAM AND ROTA AS A TYPHOON...

.NEW INFORMATION...
A Typhoon Warning has been issued for Guam, Rota, and the adjacent
waters.
A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Tinian, Saipan, and the
adjacent waters.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended action for
people on Guam, and people on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Warning is in effect for Guam and Rota.
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Tinian and Saipan.
A Typhoon Watch continues for Tinian and Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for all of Guam and the Northern Marianas.
Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might be in effect
for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 200 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 11.4N and longitude 153.3E, about 300 miles north-
northeast of Chuuk and about 590 miles east-southeast of Guam. Storm
motion was west, 265 degrees, at 24 mph. Storm intensity was 50 mph.
Champi will continue on this trajectory and slow down as it continues
barreling toward the Marianas. This general forecast track will take
Champi close to, or over, Guam Sunday morning. Champi is forecast to
continue intensifying over the next few days, likely becoming a
typhoon by Saturday.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Mostly benign conditions are expected across the Marianas tonight,
followed by a steady increase in showers and winds Friday afternoon,
and then deteriorating significantly coming into Saturday night as
Tropical Storm Champi continues to move in from the east-southeast.
Champi is expected to go through a period of rapid intensification
over the next 24 hours, becoming a typhoon by Saturday and
strengthening further thereafter. Winds and rain will come in
rapidly, with winds becoming dangerous and life threatening very soon
after onset. Do not let a false sense of normalcy now dictate your
actions tomorrow; prepare NOW!
properties.instruction:
Take small loose objects indoors. Identify suitable shelter. Stock
up a few days worth of food and water. If no concrete shelter is
available look for a cave or something similar. Take action to
protect food crops or other possessions as appropriate.

properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The second round of heavy rain is expected to bring an additional
0.5 to 1.5 inches tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end
QPF amounts expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More
localized lower or higher amounts are possible due to terrain
effects.

panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.
